 1               P R O C E E D I N G S

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   The 

 3   Senate will come to order.  

 4                I ask all present to please stand 

 5   and join with me as we recite the Pledge of 

 6   Allegiance to our Flag.

 7                (Whereupon, the assemblage recited 

 8   the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

 9                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Today's 

10   invocation will be offered by Dr. James A. 

11   Lewis, III, senior pastor, Miracle Missions Full 

12   Gospel Church in Buffalo, New York.  

13                Pastor?

14                REVEREND LEWIS:   Let us pray.

15                God of Time and Eternity, help us 

16   to look to the past with gratitude and to the 

17   future with hope.  Let us remember those who 

18   have gone before us here, who labored not for 

19   themselves alone, but with visions of building 

20   for the future of a better world than they had 

21   ever known before, inspiring us also, like a 

22   vision, that we too may labor for things beyond 

23   ourselves, that our lives may be dedicated to 

24   high purposes and grand horizons.  

25                Make us unafraid of hopes and 


                                                                621

 1   dreams.  Release us from cynicism and despair.  

 2   Teach us to be realistic about our limitations, 

 3   but never lose hope in our potential to 

 4   transcend them.  

 5                Heavenly Father, teach us to use 

 6   our freedom to help preserve and strengthen the 

 7   freedom of all by respecting and upholding its 

 8   laws, by supporting our law enforcement 

 9   agencies, by informing ourselves on current 

10   issues, by voting wisely, by respecting the 

11   differences of others, by honoring the rights of 

12   all people, asking for an end to AIDS and gun 

13   violence.  

14                We seek blessings on the task 

15   before this Senate.  Bless their efforts with 

16   clear insight and wisdom on every deliberation 

17   that they make for our community and state.  May 

18   they use their best skills and judgment, keeping 

19   themselves impartial and neutral, acting in 

20   accordance with what is best for our fellow 

21   citizens.  And may their own personal faiths 

22   give them strength to act honestly and well in 

23   all matters set before them.  

24                Now come, Holy spirit, come.

25                Amen.

22                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

23   Resolution Number 3943, by Senator Kennedy, 

24   commending Reverend Dr. James A. Lewis III upon 

25   the occasion of being named the January 2016 Erie 


                                                                624

 1   County Citizen of the Month by the Erie County 

 2   Legislature on January 21, 2016.

 3                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 4   Kennedy.

 5                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Thank you, 

 6   Mr. President.  

 7                Today I rise to honor a man who's 

 8   dedicated his life to the church and our 

 9   community, the Reverend Dr. James A. Lewis III.  

10   We all just heard from him.  He gave a truly 

11   inspiring invocation here this afternoon.  And he 

12   was recently honored as the Erie County Citizen 

13   of the Month, a well-deserved honor.  

14                I'd also like to recognize the 

15   lovely wife of Pastor Lewis of nearly 34 years, 

16   Zandra Lewis, who also made the trip today to 

17   Albany on this special occasion.  They have eight 

18   children together, many of them adopted, showing 

19   the caring and love Reverend Lewis and his wife 

20   both share.

21                Reverend Lewis was called to his 

22   ministry in 1988, after he noticed a pressing 

23   need for more people to serve.  He received a 

24   doctorate in philosophy from the University of 

25   St. Moritz, in London, before being ordained a 


                                                                625

 1   bishop and beginning his long service to the 

 2   Buffalo region.  

 3                Reverend Lewis is an extraordinary 

 4   man, a man that feels it's his duty to use his 

 5   God-given talents to help people in need.  He 

 6   understands that it's much better to live life 

 7   bringing change from the inside instead of 

 8   sitting on the sidelines.  He's dedicated to the 

 9   belief that it's better to be the change that you 

10   want to see instead of waiting and hoping that 

11   change just happens to take place.

12                You can see his dedication in his 

13   church, Miracle Mission Full Gospel Church in 

14   Buffalo, where his community of faithful gather 

15   each week to hear his preaching and to seek out 

16   the wise advice and counsel.

17                He has a special gift, and those of 

18   us here that know him, and those in the community 

19   that know him well, know that that gift is of 

20   interjecting humor into his ministry that not 

21   only magnifies his personality, but it engages 

22   his congregation, both in the church and in the 

23   community.

24                You see his dedication through his 

25   community service.  Since 1990, he's been 


                                                                626

 1   director of pastoral care for the Erie County 

 2   Medical Center.  He's a certified chief master 

 3   chaplain for the Buffalo Police Department.  He 

 4   is involved with the Upstate New York Transplant 

 5   Services, otherwise known as UNYTS, and the 

 6   founder of both the Vaughn House Shelter for Men 

 7   and G.R.O.U.P. Ministries.  Also, he's chair of 

 8   the City of Buffalo Zoning Board of Appeals, he's 

 9   chair of the Black Leadership Commission on AIDS, 

10   he's part of the board of directors of the Legal 

11   Aid Society, the Buffalo Philharmonic, the United 

12   Way of Western New York, just to name a few.  

13                There's really not a hat that Pastor 

14   Lewis hasn't worn.  And it's all to benefit other 

15   people, it's all to help other people and to help 

16   the community.  A true leader in our midst.  

17                And a little known fact about Pastor 

18   Lewis is that back in his heyday, he was a radio 

19   DJ.  Some of you may know him or have heard his 

20   work as The Love Man.  Well, today he's spreading 

21   that love in other ways, through service to the 

22   community.  

23                You can see his dedication through 

24   music.  Reverend Lewis sees beauty and healing in 

25   song, believing that barriers in this world can 


                                                                627

 1   be removed through music.  He speaks fondly of 

 2   his 10 years assisting the Buffalo Philharmonic, 

 3   proud of the tremendous growth of public 

 4   appreciation the orchestra has experienced in 

 5   that time.  He's incorporated music into his 

 6   addiction recovery services, proud of the fact 

 7   that many people have successfully treated their 

 8   addiction through the power of song.  

 9                All of these selfless acts of 

10   dedication add up to show how truly remarkable 

11   Reverend Lewis is and how much of an asset he is 

12   to Buffalo, Western New York, and New York State.  

13                Pastor Lewis, First Lady, we all owe 

14   you and your leadership and your family a 

15   tremendous debt of gratitude for all that you've 

16   given to each and every one of us and what you've 

17   bestowed on our community.  

18                Congratulations on being named the 

19   Erie County Citizen of the Month, and it is 

20   extremely well deserved.  I believe that you 

21   should get this award every single month, Pastor.  

22   For our sake and for Buffalo's sake, please keep 

23   up the great work.  

24                Mr. President, I vote aye on this 

25   resolution.  I would ask that this resolution be 


                                                                628

 1   opened up for each and every one of us to 

 2   cosponsor.  And if you could offer the honor of 

 3   the house to Pastor Lewis and First Lady Zandra 

 4   Lewis.  

 5                Thank you, Mr. President.

10                First let me begin by thanking 

11   Senator Kennedy for his leadership and 

12   recognizing one of the great men, not just of 

13   Erie County or Buffalo, but of the State of 

14   New York.  

15                Reverend James A. Lewis III -- I 

16   didn't know The Love Man -- is really, really an 

17   outstanding individual.  And for me to be a state 

18   legislator from Brooklyn, to have a relationship 

19   and knowledge of his work, you know how great it 

20   is.  He's somebody who is an exemplar, not just 

21   in the Buffalo community or the Erie County 

22   community, but in the State of New York.  

23                I have gotten to know Reverend Lewis 

24   in my work with Buffalo.  And, you know, 

25   particularly last year we shared a dais as I got

 1   the opportunity to be the keynote speaker at the 

 2   Grassroots Dinner in Buffalo, New York.  

 3                And so I've had an opportunity to 

 4   visit his congregation numbers of years ago 

 5   during my tenure with H. Carl McCall, when he was 

 6   the State Comptroller and I was in his employ, 

 7   and since then I have watched the amazing work

 9                I think that Senator Kennedy, in all 

10   of the things that he talked about, talked about 

11   the kind of a renaissance man that Pastor Lewis 

12   is.  And what he gives every single day made me 

13   tired just hearing all of the work that he's

15   he's doing and really push him to continue to do 

16   that kind of work again and share your gifts with 

17   the world.

18                Thank you so much for all that you 

19   do, and certainly you're a great example and a 

20   great benefit to the people of not just Buffalo 

21   and not just your church, but certainly to the 

22   people of the State of New York.

23   Resolution Number 3895, by Senator Peralta, 

24   commemorating the 172nd Anniversary of the 

25   Dominican Republic Independence to be celebrated 


                                                                631

 1   on February 27, 2016.

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 3   Peralta.

 4                SENATOR PERALTA:   Thank you, 

 5   Mr. President.  

 6                2016 marks the 172nd anniversary of 

 7   the Dominican Republic independence.  It occurred 

 8   on February 27, 1844.  A few years before that, 

 9   in 1838, Juan Pablo Duarte, the nation's 

10   patriarch, formed La Trinitaria, a secret society 

11   founded with the objective of gaining 

12   independence from Haiti.  

13                Duarte was joined by Matías Mella 

14   and Rosario Sánchez.  The same way American 

15   independence is closely identified with the 

16   fearless leadership of George Washington, Ben 

17   Franklin, Thomas Jefferson and John Adams, 

18   Dominican independence would be remiss not to 

19   recognize La Trinitaria y los Trinitarios.  

20                Six years after its formation, the 

21   Trinitarios declared independence from Haiti.  

22   That same year, in 1844, the Dominican Republic 

23   adopted its first constitution.  

24                Duarte's historical significance is 

25   evident.  Some of the noteworthy landmarks 


                                                                632

 1   honoring Juan Pablo Duarte are Pico Duarte, which 

 2   is the highest mountain in the Caribbean, and 

 3   Duarte Square, which is located in a park in 

 4   New York City.

 5                We celebrate Dominican independence, 

 6   and we also celebrate the many contributions 

 7   Dominicans and Dominican-Americans have made to 

 8   our city, to our state, and to our nation.  And 

 9   in fact, Dominican-Americans are participating in 

10   a larger number in the electoral process in the 

11   State of New York, as evident by the rising 

12   number of Dominican electeds here not only in the 

13   Senate, but also in the New York State Assembly 

14   and in the City Council of New York City -- but 

15   also because of their contributions to the arts, 

16   the economy, culture, forming part of our great 

17   mosaic that defines our diversity, contributions 

18   that have enriched our lives and the lives of so 

19   many others.  

20                Through their vital contributions 

21   and tireless work, Dominicans and 

22   Dominican-Americans have strengthened our 

23   communities, our neighborhoods and our economy.  

24                I am proud to stand here celebrating 

25   the pride of being a Dominicano as we commemorate 


                                                                633

 1   our 172nd anniversary as a nation.  By way of 

 2   this resolution, we extend our best wishes to our 

 3   Dominican-American friends throughout New York 

 4   City and across New York State.  

 5                Thank you, Mr. President.
